Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need help turning this into a clear prompt for a pickup-day plan, not the plan itself yet. this is a return parcel being collected from our house, not a delivery to us. the booking is for thursday 19 june, with the carrier's collection window listed as 2 pm to 6 pm. the address on the booking is 8 Alder Row. the booking reference is H7Q4 and the tracking number ends in 3816. i want the prompt to ask for something practical that Nora and Eli can use, because we have been discussing the handoff in separate messages and keep losing the important timing detail.

The parcel is already packed. It is a shoe box inside a plain brown carton, about 43 by 31 by 18 centimetres and 2.4 kilograms. The prepaid carrier label is attached flat to the top, and the brown tape is sealed along the main opening. The booking says the label needs to be attached and does not ask us to print anything else or show a QR code. There is only this one parcel for collection; don't make it sound like the driver is picking up other boxes or delivering something at the same time. It is currently indoors in the hall, beside the low cabinet, not outside by the door. It should stay there until somebody can hand it over.

Nora works from home that morning but has to leave at 3:15 pm. Eli is expected back from work at around 4:10 pm, though traffic can delay him, and he may not get back before 4:30. Either of them can answer the front door if actually home. The doorbell works and is on the right side of the front door. The collection window goes on until 6, but nobody should assume one of us will be available throughout the whole window. The point we need stated clearly is this: if the courier arrives before 4:30 pm and Nora or Eli is home and able to answer, hand the parcel directly to the courier. If that condition is not met—because the arrival is at or after 4:30, or because neither of us is home to answer at an earlier time—do not leave the parcel outside; keep it indoors and use the carrier app to request another weekday collection. Please make the two branches explicit, not just a vague line saying to arrange pickup when possible. The difference between before 4:30 and at 4:30 matters.

There is a small dog, Miso, who can get to the area by the side gate if the parcel is left there. The side gate is not a collection point, and we shouldn't tell a courier or a neighbour to put the carton there. The porch is also exposed to rain. Eli wrote in the household chat, “Please don't leave it by the gate; the dog can reach that area.” Nora said, “It has to be collected from the address on the booking.” Those are just the practical things they already said, not new instructions from the carrier. The parcel can be carried from the hall to the front door when someone is there, but don't suggest moving it outside in advance or putting it beside the bins.

A few booking details from the email should be reflected without making up a carrier policy. The collection is attached to the address above, and the label already has that address and the return information. The booking email is on Nora's phone, and she can forward it to Eli before she leaves. If the driver asks to see the booking confirmation, the person answering can show that email on the phone. We don't have a pickup signature requirement written in the booking, so don't say that a signature is required or that it isn't required. We also have no information about the driver's exact arrival time, whether they will call first, or whether the app will offer a particular slot. Don't guess about any of those.

The timing is a little easy to muddle because the window runs past the time Eli may get home. Nora will leave the carton in the hall before she goes, and Eli should check whether it is still there when he gets home. If he is already home when the driver comes before 4:30, he can take it to the front door and hand it over; if he is not back in time, the fallback still applies. Nora can send him the reference and the email, but she cannot stay home after 3:15. Don't phrase the fallback as if the courier has already missed the pickup, since this is a plan for Thursday and we do not know what will happen.

There was also a brief call to the carrier's general support line when we were checking the booking. The person on the phone said, “If you miss us, we'll have to book again.” We were not given a phone number for the driver or a way to change the pickup window during the day. The useful fallback we actually have is to request another weekday collection through the carrier app. If nobody is available under the stated condition, the carton should stay indoors rather than be left at the gate or on the porch, and the app request can be made after that. Don't turn the support person's quote into a guarantee about what the app will offer.

Could the resulting prompt ask for a short, clear household pickup-day checklist and a brief message Nora can send Eli? We need the checklist to cover checking the parcel and label, the hall location, who may answer the door, and what to do in each timing case. In the numbered section, keep the main handoff rule as item 1 and the no-one-available alternative as item 2; those are the two actions that must not get blended together. Include the booking window, date, address, reference, tracking ending, and parcel dimensions so the prompt has enough detail to be useful. Keep the exact quoted sentences above, and keep the output framed as a plan to use before the collection, not as a report that the pickup happened. Don't add a confirmed pickup, a new appointment, or a recommendation beyond the details here.

One last thing for the prompt: ask that the final part remind us not to mark the return as collected until the parcel has actually been handed to the courier. If it is handed over, whoever is there can update Nora and Eli in the household chat afterward; if it is not handed over, the parcel stays inside and the app is used for the next weekday collection request. Those are conditional next steps, not two things to do at once. Keep that distinction in the final part, and don't end by saying everything is sorted, because we haven't reached Thursday yet.", "output": "Create a practical pickup-day plan for Nora and Eli for the return parcel collection described below. The plan is for use before the collection; do not imply that the parcel has already been picked up or that a new appointment has been arranged. Include a short household checklist and a brief message Nora can send Eli.

**Booking and parcel details**
- Collection date: Thursday 19 June.
- Collection window: 2 pm to 6 pm.
- Address on the booking: 8 Alder Row.
- Booking reference: H7Q4.
- Tracking number ending: 3816.
- The parcel is a shoe box inside a plain brown carton, approximately 43 by 31 by 18 centimetres and 2.4 kilograms.
- The prepaid carrier label is attached flat to the top, and the brown tape seals the main opening. The booking says the label needs to be attached; it does not ask for anything else to be printed or for a QR code to be shown. There is only one parcel for collection, not other boxes or a delivery.

The parcel is indoors in the hall beside the low cabinet. Keep it there until someone can hand it over. Nora works from home that morning but leaves at 3:15 pm. Eli is expected home from work around 4:10 pm, but traffic may delay him, and he may not be back before 4:30. Either can answer the front door if actually home. The doorbell works and is on the right side of the front door. Do not assume either person is available for the whole collection window.

**Numbered handoff instructions**
1. If the courier arrives before 4:30 pm and Nora or Eli is home and able to answer, take the parcel from the hall and hand it directly to the courier at the front door.
2. If that condition is not met—if the courier arrives at or after 4:30 pm, or arrives earlier when neither Nora nor Eli is home to answer—do not leave the parcel outside. Keep it indoors and use the carrier app to request another weekday collection. Make the two branches and their conditions explicit; the distinction between before 4:30 and at 4:30 matters.

Nora will leave the carton in the hall before she goes. Eli should check whether it is still there when he gets home. If he is home when the courier arrives before 4:30, he can bring it to the front door and hand it over; if he is not back in time, use the fallback above. Nora can forward Eli the booking email before she leaves, but she cannot stay home after 3:15.

**Location and booking information**
Miso, the small dog, can reach the area by the side gate. That gate is not a collection point; do not suggest leaving the parcel there or asking a courier or neighbour to put it there. The porch is exposed to rain. The parcel may be carried from the hall to the front door when someone is there, but do not suggest placing it outside in advance or beside the bins. Eli said, “Please don't leave it by the gate; the dog can reach that area.” Nora said, “It has to be collected from the address on the booking.” Keep these as the household’s stated practical concerns, not as additional carrier instructions.

The booking email is on Nora’s phone, and she can forward it to Eli. If the driver asks to see the booking confirmation, the person answering can show the email on a phone. The booking does not state whether a pickup signature is required, so do not claim either that one is required or that it is not. The driver’s exact arrival time, whether they will call first, and whether the app will offer a particular time slot are unknown; do not guess.

The carrier’s general support line said, “If you miss us, we'll have to book again.” No driver phone number or way to change the pickup window during the day was provided. The available fallback is to request another weekday collection through the carrier app. If nobody is available under the stated condition, keep the carton indoors and make the app request; do not present the quote as a guarantee about what the app will offer.

In the checklist, cover checking the parcel and label, its location in the hall, who may answer, and both timing branches. Include the date, window, address, booking reference, tracking number ending, and parcel dimensions. Keep the main handoff rule as item 1 and the no-one-available alternative as item 2, without blending the actions together.

In the final part, remind Nora and Eli not to mark the return as collected until the parcel has actually been handed to the courier. If it is handed over, the person there can update them both in the household chat afterward. If it is not handed over, the parcel stays indoors and the carrier app is used to request the next weekday collection. These are conditional next steps, not actions to take at the same time. Do not end by saying everything is sorted; the collection has not happened yet."}]
